title: Make the deploy gate decide on every canary

blocks.text: Before a build reaches every server it runs as a canary, and `DeployGate` decides whether to promote it. The gate is configured with the highest error rate it still promotes, and the release team has two complaints. With a limit of 30 %, the gate held a canary that failed 3 of its 10 requests. And last Friday it promoted a canary that had served no requests at all, because its load balancer was misconfigured, and the build broke every server it reached.

`DeployGate.judge` already turns the metrics into an error rate. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/DeployGate.java`: `allows(errorRate)` promotes a canary at or under the limit, and holds everything else, including a canary the gate has no real rate for. `DeployGate.TOLERANCE` is there for you to use.

cases.says: a canary well under the limit is promoted, and one well over it is held
a canary whose error rate is exactly the limit is promoted, although the computed rate is a rounding error above it
a canary that served no requests, whose rate is NaN, is held

origin.section: Integer Division by Zero Throws; Floating-Point Division Returns Infinity or NaN, and NaN Equals Nothing

concepts: A double holds a binary fraction, so computed values are compared with a tolerance, not ==.
Floating-point division by zero returns Infinity or NaN, and every comparison with NaN is false, so !(x > limit) is not x <= limit.
